purpose: Compiler acceptance and rejection probes for Swift 6.4 type-system boundaries.
interpretation: expected_success means expected compiler acceptance, not correctness, runtime safety, or recommended use. Expected rejections require the stated diagnostic substring. All sources are compiled independently.

probes.name: integer_shape_valid
probes.note: Corrected shape-compatible composition and same-value extension. Replaces the initial redundant-equivalence trial.

probes.name: integer_shape_invalid
probes.expected_diagnostic_contains: cannot convert value of type 'Matrix<4, 5>' to expected argument type 'Matrix<3, 5>'

probes.name: inline_array_valid
integer_arithmetic_default
probes.expected_diagnostic_contains: expected type
probes.source:
struct Sized<let N: Int> {}
func expression() { let _: Sized<(2 + 3)> = .init() }

probes.name: integer_constant_default
probes.expected_diagnostic_contains: cannot find type 'count' in scope
probes.source:

func expression() { let count = 5; let _: Sized<count> = .init() }

probes.name: integer_generic_arithmetic
probes.expected_diagnostic_contains: expected type
probes.source:
struct Sized<let N: Int> {}
func append<let N: Int>(_ x: Sized<N>) -> Sized<(N + 1)> { .init() }

probes.name: integer_inequality_constraint
probes.expected_diagnostic_contains: expected ':' or '==' to indicate a conformance or same-type requirement
probes.source:
struct Sized<let N: Int> {}
func positive<let N: Int>(_ x: Sized<N>) where N > 0 {}

probes.name: inline_array_hashable
probes.expected_diagnostic_contains: global function 'requiresHash' requires that '[3 of Int]' conform to 'Hashable'

func tuple() { let a: [3 of Int] = [1, 2, 3]; requiresHash(a) }

probes.name: custom_lifetime_default
probes.expected_diagnostic_contains: a function cannot return a ~Escapable result
probes.source:
@_lifetime(borrow values)
func dependent(_ values: borrowing [Int]) -> Span<Int> { values.span }

probes.name: yielding_accessors
probes.expected_diagnostic_contains: 'yielding borrow' accessor is only valid when experimental feature coroutine accessors is enabled
probes.source: struct Holder { var storage: Int; var value: Int { yielding borrow { yield storage } } }

probes.name: safe_raw_bytes
probes.source: func read(_ bytes: RawSpan) -> UInt32 { bytes.load(fromByteOffset: 0, as: UInt32.self) }

probes.name: span_single_value
probes.expected_diagnostic_contains: incorrect argument label in call (have 'borrowing:', expected 'viewing:')
probes.source: func single(_ value: borrowing Int) { let span = Span(borrowing: value); _ = span.count }

probes.name: inline_array_wrong_arity
probes.expected_diagnostic_contains: expected '3' elements in inline array literal, but got '2'
probes.source: func example() { let _: [3 of Int] = [1, 2] }

probes.name: inline_array_unchecked_index
probes.note: Acceptance means no static index-range proof. This subscript retains a runtime check; it was not executed.
probes.source: func example(_ values: [3 of Int]) -> Int { values[100] }

probes.name: inline_array_negative_size
probes.note: Acceptance is at SIL emission only; it does not assert valid layout or runtime construction for negative size.
probes.source: func example(_ values: [-1 of Int]) {}

probes.name: span_getter_valid
probes.expected_diagnostic_contains: a method cannot return a ~Escapable result
probes.note: The forwarding getter is semantically plausible but rejected in default mode because custom nonescapable returns require Lifetimes.
probes.source: struct Bytes { var storage: [UInt8]; var span: Span<UInt8> { storage.span } }

probes.name: span_getter_escape_invalid
probes.expected_diagnostic_contains: a method cannot return a ~Escapable result
probes.note: Default-mode rejection is a feature gate. Use span_local_escape_explicit_lifetime to verify the actual escape rule.
probes.source: struct Bytes { var span: Span<UInt8> { let local: [UInt8] = [1, 2]; return local.span } }

probes.source: func dependent(_ values: borrowing [Int]) -> Span<Int> { values.span }

probes.name: literal_expression_experimental
probes.expected_diagnostic_contains: unsupported operator in a literal expression
probes.note: Uses the exact parenthesized SE-0531 syntax, not the unsupported unparenthesized spelling.
probes.source:
struct Sized<let N: Int> {}
func expression() { let _: Sized<(2 + 3)> = .init() }

probes.name: negative_inline_array_init
probes.note: Acceptance is at SIL emission only; this program was not linked or executed.

probes.name: deinit_mutation
probes.expected_diagnostic_contains: left side of mutating operator isn't mutable: 'self' is immutable
probes.source: struct Resource: ~Copyable { var value: Int; deinit { value += 1 } }

probes.name: span_getter_lifetimes
probes.source: struct Bytes { var storage: [Int]; var span: Span<Int> { storage.span } }

probes.name: span_getter_escape_lifetimes
probes.expected_diagnostic_contains: cannot infer lifetime dependence on a method because 'self' is BitwiseCopyable, specify '@_lifetime(borrow self)'
probes.note: Checks refusal to infer a borrow from BitwiseCopyable self; the explicit-owner escape test checks actual lifetime violation.
probes.source: struct Bytes { var span: Span<Int> { let local = [1,2,3]; return local.span } }

probes.name: span_local_escape_explicit_lifetime
probes.expected_diagnostic_contains: lifetime-dependent value escapes its scope
probes.note: With Lifetimes enabled and an explicit owner dependency, a span of unrelated local storage must still be rejected.
